intelligent_control.benchmarks.caption: Section 3.1 — Artificial system identification problems. Exact SISO and two-output recurrences, delay memory, excitation and independent evaluation. This family contains two implemented examples, not a physical vessel.

Section 3.2 — Data repositories for system identification and regression. The seven data resources named in the survey and the provenance, split and import contract. This is a resource category, not a plant model.
Section 3.3 — Cart with inverted pendulum. Cart, applied force, angular convention, sensors, mechanical coupling and the four-state implementation.

Section 3.4 — Electro-mechanical throttle. Duty-cycle command, motor, transmission, spring, throttle plate and angle measurement. Original measured training/test records remain unavailable; a physical diagram does not replace them.

Section 3.5 — Servo-pneumatic actuator. Vertical actuator, payload gravity, chambers, valve paths, gas mass/energy states and derived pressures. The literal survey transcription and the separate physical interpretation remain distinct.

Section 3.6 — Hydrostatic transmission in mobile working machines. Pump/motor, closed hydraulic loop, displacement commands, pressure storage, losses and mechanical load. The SI interpretation states its units and assumptions; historical calibration is still unresolved.
Section 3.7 — Three-tank-system. The physical T1-T3-T2 order, signed inter-tank flows, nominal closed drains, pumps and level measurements.
Section 3.8 — Continuously operated bio-chemical reactor. Mixing, dilution, equal feed/outlet flows, growth/conversion states and sampled command path.

Section 3.9 — Continuously stirred chemical reactor. Jacketed vessel, desired and undesired reaction paths, concentration/temperature states and separate dilution/cooling inputs, retaining the audited Celsius convention.

Section 3.10 — Continuously operated binary distillation column. 41 stages and 82 states, feed at stage 21, condenser/reboiler, reflux/boilup, products and inventory loops. The 4-input plant and 2-input LV interpretation are explicitly distinguished.

Section 3.11 — ALSTOM Gasifier Control Benchmark II. The five commanded mass flows, four outputs, two disturbances and fixed limestone/coal ratio. A qualitative vessel supports the documented control interface, without inventing proprietary internal hardware.

Section 3.12 — Wind turbine. Rotor, blades, tower, drivetrain, generator, pitch actuator and nine reduced states. The reduced model, later ROSCO aerodynamic map and full aeroelastic simulator remain identified as different variants.

Section 3.13 — Tennessee Eastman process control problem. Five process units, 11 numbered process streams, compressor bypass, purge, cooling and steam utilities, valves and measurement groups. The companion sheet maps all 12 manipulated variables and 41 standard measurements. The archived native C implementation defines 50 states; its inconsistent 52-state introductory comment is documented in the state-count audit.
Tennessee Eastman process control problem — all 12 manipulated and 41 measured variables, units, analyzer groups and version boundaries.
